messages:
Maya: Heads up — I'm planning a TF change to migrate `cache-service` from Deployment -> StatefulSet so pods keep stable network IDs for leader-election. Quick sanity check on replicas, PVC behavior, and secret rotation wiring? Plan sketch: replicas=3, `podManagementPolicy: Parallel`, `updateStrategy: RollingUpdate` with `partition=0`, keep PVC retention. Any red flags?

Jonathan: Makes sense for leader-election. A few notes: 1) If you keep PVC retention, scaling down then back up will keep previous data — fine if that's intended. 2) RollingUpdate partition=0 is normal rolling; if you need strict ordering consider `OnDelete` or `OrderedReady`. 3) Ensure headless service exists for stable DNS. :+1:

Sam: replicas=3 LGTM. Add anti-affinity so they spread across AZs/hosts (topologySpread or podAntiAffinity). Also watch readinessProbe timeouts — rolling updates can thrash the leader if probes are too aggressive.

Lina: For secret rotation — our syncer looks for annotation `redwood.com/secret-version`. After rotating secrets you need to bump an annotation on the StatefulSet template to force a rollout. Example patch: 

```
kubectl patch sts/cache-service -n prod \
  -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood.com/secret-version":"v2"}}}}}'
```

You can also set TF to update the `metadata.annotations` on template on secret change (e.g. `replace_on_change`).

infra-bot: Terraform plan preview: change detected -> `kubernetes_stateful_set.cache_service.spec.update_strategy.rolling_update.partition` 1 -> 0. No PVC recreation. No other destructive ops.

Maya: Good catch. Action items I see: add anti-affinity/topologySpread, relax/bump probe thresholds, add annotation helper for secret rotation, and pick a canary approach. Thinking to do a staged canary by setting `partition` to 2 first to leave one older pod. Thoughts?

Jonathan: For canary, setting `partition = replicas - N` works (partition keeps that many old pods). Simpler than a separate canary Deployment with shared PVCs. Monitor metrics and then set partition=0. :thinking:

Sam: Also consider changing `podManagementPolicy` to `OrderedReady` if you rely on strict ordering to avoid split-brain during failover. If the cache handles concurrent starts fine, `Parallel` is faster.

Lina: I'll open a small PR to the k8s module: add topologySpreadConstraints, a helper var to auto-bump `redwood.com/secret-version` in the module, and a note about partition-based canaries. Ping me in CR for review.

Maya: Thanks — I'll push the TF diff in ~30m and tag @Lina @Sam for review. infra-bot mark: reviewed-by=Jonathan :thumbsup:
